accounting.name: Accountants and bookkeepers
accounting.desc: Accounting, tax, audit, bookkeeping and payroll services
profile: Hold client funds or have signing authority on client bank accounts?
IRD audits or disputes handled for clients?

gen: Check the minimum professional indemnity cover and any run-off requirement set by the professional body the members belong to.
pi: Tax advice and penalties
Clients can claim for penalties and interest from wrong tax advice. Check wording on tax penalties and the excess.
Signing authority and client funds
Authority to pay from client bank accounts, trust accounts and payroll runs. Check dishonesty, crime and client-money cover.
Audit and assurance work
Audit and assurance carry higher exposure. Check any exclusion for listed entities, insolvency work or valuations.

legal.name: Law firms and lawyers
profile: Number of conveyancing transactions in a year

gen: Check the cover meets the legal profession’s regulatory requirements, including fidelity and trust account arrangements.
pi: Conveyancing and settlement
Property transactions bring settlement errors, title issues and interest claims. Check limits, excesses and any sub-limits for conveyancing.
Deadlines and limitation periods
Missed filing deadlines and limitation dates are the classic claim. Ask about diary systems and peer checks.
Cyber fraud on settlement funds
Fraudsters impersonate parties to redirect settlement funds. Check callback procedures and cover for social engineering.

it.name: IT services and software
it.desc: IT support, software and web development, programming, SaaS and web services. Technology errors and omissions (tech liability)
profile: Service level agreements with uptime or response guarantees?
Software used in critical systems such as health, finance or safety?
Contracts cap liability (e.g. to fees paid) and exclude consequential loss?
Own-built products sold or licensed to others?

pi: Limitation of liability in contracts
Standard terms should cap liability and exclude consequential loss. Check contracts with larger customers where limits are negotiated.
Outages and service levels
Service credits, uptime guarantees and downtime claims. Ask about redundancy, incident response and disaster recovery testing.
Intellectual property
Infringement claims over code, libraries and open-source licences. Check IP cover and licence management.
Tech E&O wording: what is covered

Check the policy responds to errors in software, websites and advice, failure to deliver on time, breach of contract limited to the standard of care, and defence costs. Confirm the contractual liability exclusion does not remove cover for liability assumed in customer contracts.
Retro date, claims-made and run-off
Tech E&O is claims-made. Keep the continuous retroactive date, and ask about extended reporting if cover is cancelled or the business is sold.
Cyber and tech E&O together
Many markets write tech E&O with cyber on one form. Check data breach response costs, system outage and business interruption sit alongside the professional liability limit, not eroding it.
cyber: Customer data hosted for others, breach notification duties and the response plan. A supplier breach can trigger claims from many customers at once.

consulting.name: Consultants and business advisers
consulting.desc: Management, HR, environmental and other consulting
profile: Regulated activity, such as financial advice, or advice that others rely on in lending or investment?

pi: Outcome guarantees and success fees
Guarantees of results or performance-based fees raise exposure. Check wording and exclusions for warranties and guarantees.
Reliance by third parties
Reports used by banks, investors or regulators. Ask who may rely on the work and the disclaimers used.

engineering.name: Engineers, architects and surveyors
engineering.desc: Structural, civil and building design, architecture, surveying and planning
profile: Internal peer review of design work?

pi: Building Act long-tail exposure
Claims on design can arise up to 10 years after building work. Check retroactive date, run-off cover and what happens if the firm closes.
Producer statements and reliance
Issuing producer statements means councils and others rely on the work. Ask about review, sign-off and qualifications.
Weathertightness, geotechnical and seismic
These areas generate the largest claims. Check any exclusions and the limit against the largest project.

marketing.name: Marketing, design and media
marketing.desc: Advertising, design, branding, PR, photography and digital media
profile: Handle client media spend or pay suppliers on behalf of clients?
Run competitions or promotions for clients?

pi: Copyright, defamation and false claims
Infringing images, music or text, and misleading advertising claims under the Fair Trading Act. Check media liability wording and clearance procedures.
Client money and media buying
Paying media suppliers on a client’s behalf creates credit and fraud risk. Check crime cover and terms.

recruitment.name: Recruitment and labour hire
recruitment.desc: Recruitment agencies, labour hire and contracting services
profile: Average number of temporary staff placed at any time
Annual wages paid to temporary staff
Health and safety responsibilities agreed in writing with host employers?

liab: Injury and property damage caused by placed workers. Check who controls the work, written agreements and the host employer’s insurance.
pi: Placement guarantees and fee refunds
Guarantee periods and refunds on failed placements. Check how these are treated and the claims history.
Vetting and references
Wrong or missing checks on qualifications and criminal history. Check processes and records.
statutory: Health and safety, holiday pay and minimum wage compliance for placed workers. Check regulator history and defence cost cover.

realestate.name: Real estate agents and property managers
realestate.desc: Real estate agencies, salespeople and property management
profile: Agency and all salespeople licensed, with certificates current?

gen: Agency licence, salespeople licensed under the Real Estate Agents Act 2008 and any complaints or disciplinary matters.
pi: Disclosure of defects
Defects, weathertightness, contamination and consents not disclosed. Ask about vendor information, LIM checks and file notes.
Property management errors
Tenancy bond handling, rent collection errors and failing to act on repairs. Check Residential Tenancies Act exposure.
crime: Deposit money, rent and bonds held in trust. Check dual authorisation, reconciliations and dishonesty cover.

financial.name: Mortgage brokers and financial advisers
financial.desc: Financial advice providers, mortgage and insurance advisers
profile: Financial advice provider licence held, and a dispute resolution scheme member?
Funds under advice or loan book size

gen: Financial advice provider licence, nominated representatives, the code of conduct and dispute resolution membership. Check the policy matches the licence conditions.
pi: Advice records and suitability
Claims arise when advice or disclosure is missing or unsuitable. Ask about advice documents, file notes and product replacement.
Claims-made and run-off
Advice can be challenged years later. Check retroactive date and run-off when advisers leave or retire.

property.name: Property investors and landlords
property.desc: Owners of commercial, industrial and residential rental property
profile: Building warrant of fitness current where required?
Earthquake-prone notice or seismic rating below 34% NBS?
Asbestos, combustible cladding or defective materials known?

gen: Check leases require tenants to carry liability cover, and who insures fit-out, glass and signage.
Long vacancy triggers conditions and exclusions. Ask about inspections, services and security.
mdamage: Recent valuation, code upgrade costs, demolition and professional fees. Older and heritage buildings often need specialist valuation.
Flood, slip, coastal and earthquake exposure and the cover available for natural disaster damage. Seismic assessments affect insurer appetite.
bi: Rent roll, indemnity period and rent review dates. Rebuilds and consents can take 18 months or more.
liab: Slips, trips and falls in common areas, and works by tenants. Check contractor controls and consent for alterations.
